chapter: Violinists, Jimmy Noon and Decatur Street
title: Boots and Sport Young, and boogie-woogie in early bands
summary: Interviewer names Sport and Boots Young; Bourgeau says early bands played boogie-woogie blues and Dixieland, with violin, piano, banjo and bass.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: I'm getting here. I'm getting here. I'm getting here. I'm getting here. What are they? Let's see. They had Louie Nelson. They had Sport Young and Boots Young. I'm not going to do it, Nelson. Not the Youngs. Boots and Sport. They played? They played.
Yeah. What a big deal. He was dark? Boots was dark and he was real little-looking. A skinny-looking guy. But he was real strong.
Yeah. He switched to bass later on. Oh, in Monopakia? He was playing the taxi dance.
I know. There's plenty of fellas you've heard of and never seen them.
Yeah. Did they ever have any good boogie-woogie players in them?

Oh, man, that's all he had around. Boogie-woogie! Talk about this boogie-woogie stuff. That's all them fellas used to play around here one time. Boogie-woogie. Who played it? All them little bands. We played it, too. You mean in a band or what? Yeah, they played in a band. That's music. Boogie-woogie music. They're still playing it. That's how we played it, sir. Dixieland. We played nothing else but Dixieland. I mean, when you started out, way in the early, early days, did they play boogie or something?

That's all we used to play, boogie-woogie. And violin played sound like a saxophone. We had violin, we had piano, we had banjo, and we had bass. I'd have forgot who was playing the bass. We used to play all the boogie-woogie notes. You know, the ones that they had. Blues and them boogie-woogie blues, we still play that. I'd call them still play that. Thomas, Leroy. Yeah. Every nine minutes, we shoves them out, you know? Yeah. And that second line, oh man, we were talking about that second line. That's how the theme song, second line.
